card.name: Start of an instruction or audience sentence
card.fires_on: The word right where a new sentence or clause begins, often "students" or "Patients" as the subject, or a colon or period before an instruction. It shows up in lesson plans and drug labels.

modes.label: Students as subject
modes.description: The word "students" starts the clause in a lesson-plan summary, just before a verb like complete or discover.
modes.example: In this Native people of Alaska lesson plan,<< students>> discover the three groups of people who live

modes.label: Patient(s) at sentence start
modes.description: "Patient" or "Patients" opens a new sentence or heading in a drug label.
modes.example: to XELJANZ XR Extended-Release Tablets<< Patients>> treated with XELJANZ tablets

modes.label: Punctuation before a task
modes.description: A colon or period that ends a step and leads into the next instruction.
modes.example: Step Two<<:>> Complete the Shape Activities at the end
